check: The agreement type and billing account are confirmed, with at least two named billing owners.
why_it_matters: Billing set up late or by one person blocks subscriptions and invoices.
evidence_to_collect: Billing account screenshot or export, owner list.

check: The decision to reuse the existing Microsoft Entra tenant or create a new one is recorded with the reasons.
why_it_matters: A second tenant is hard to merge later and splits identity and licensing.

check: At least two people hold the highest tenant and billing roles, and the roles are reviewed.
why_it_matters: One person leaving or being unavailable must not lock the organisation out.

check: Invoice routing, purchase order handling and cost centre mapping are agreed with finance.
why_it_matters: Invoices that nobody recognises or can code get disputed or paid late.

check: The management group hierarchy is designed and documented (platform, workload landing zones, sandbox, decommissioned).
why_it_matters: The hierarchy is where policy and access are inherited. Redesigning it later moves everything.

check: The subscription design is agreed (for example one per workload environment or per team) and service limits were checked.
why_it_matters: Subscriptions are the unit of scale, billing and isolation.

check: A naming standard and a required tag set (owner, cost centre, environment, criticality, data classification) are published.
why_it_matters: Without tags, cost and ownership questions cannot be answered later.

check: Primary and secondary regions are chosen with data residency and latency in mind.
why_it_matters: Region is hard to change once data and dependencies are in place.

check: The identity source of truth is decided and synchronisation from the on premises directory to Microsoft Entra ID works.
why_it_matters: Identity is the main security boundary in the cloud and every other design depends on it.

check: Multifactor authentication is enforced for all administrators, and baseline Conditional Access policies are in place.
why_it_matters: Administrator accounts are the most valuable target.

check: Privileged access is role based with just-in-time elevation (for example Privileged Identity Management), no standing owner rights, and scheduled access reviews.
why_it_matters: Standing high privilege turns one stolen credential into a full breach.

check: Emergency access accounts exist, are excluded from policies that could lock them out, are monitored, and were tested.
why_it_matters: A policy mistake must not lock everyone out of the tenant.

check: Workloads use managed identities or service principals with a named owner, and no shared administrator passwords exist.
why_it_matters: Shared credentials cannot be traced or rotated safely.

check: Role assignments are made to groups, not individuals, with named group owners.
why_it_matters: Individual assignments are never cleaned up.

check: Where lifted applications need domain join, domain controllers or an equivalent service are available in Azure and tested.
why_it_matters: Many legacy applications fail without a reachable directory.

check: The IP address plan is agreed, does not overlap with on premises, partner or other cloud networks, and leaves room to grow.
why_it_matters: Overlap blocks connectivity and re-addressing is painful.

check: The topology (for example hub and spoke, or Virtual WAN) is chosen and the reasons are recorded.
why_it_matters: Topology determines routing, inspection and cost.

check: Hybrid connectivity (private circuit and or VPN) is in place with a resilient path, and bandwidth was sized from the dependency flows.
why_it_matters: Every wave leaves some links crossing between on premises and Azure.
evidence_to_collect: Circuit order, throughput test, failover test.

check: Name resolution works in both directions between on premises and Azure, including private zones.
why_it_matters: Broken DNS is the most common cause of a failed cutover.

check: Central filtering (firewall or network virtual appliance), internet egress and ingress rules are designed and reviewed.
why_it_matters: Traffic leaving or entering the estate needs one controlled path.

check: Segmentation (network security groups, separation by environment and data sensitivity) is designed and tested.
why_it_matters: Flat networks let a single compromise spread.

check: Latency and bandwidth were measured for every pair of applications that will straddle the boundary between waves.
why_it_matters: A call that took 1 ms on one network can take far longer across a link.

check: Administrator and user remote access avoids public management ports.
why_it_matters: Exposed management ports are attacked within hours.

check: A security baseline for Azure is approved, with named owners for approving and monitoring it.
why_it_matters: Standards without owners decay.

check: Cloud security posture management (for example Microsoft Defender for Cloud) is enabled for all subscriptions and recommendations are triaged.
why_it_matters: Misconfiguration is the common cause of cloud breaches.

check: Encryption at rest and in transit defaults are set, and the approach to keys (for example Azure Key Vault, customer managed keys or not) is decided.
why_it_matters: Key decisions are expensive to reverse.

check: Endpoint protection and vulnerability scanning cover migrated virtual machines.
why_it_matters: Migrated machines often arrive with old agents or none.

check: Security logs flow to a central workspace and the security team's tooling, with retention agreed.
why_it_matters: Logs not collected from day one cannot be recovered after an incident.

check: The incident response plan covers Azure resources: who acts, how to isolate a workload, and how to contact the provider.
why_it_matters: A plan written for on premises does not say how to isolate a cloud workload.

check: A data protection review is complete for applications holding high or restricted data, with region and residency recorded.
why_it_matters: Moving personal or regulated data without a review can breach obligations.

check: Third party access (vendors, managed service providers) has a defined route, role and expiry.
why_it_matters: Standing supplier access is a common weak point.
evidence_to_collect: Access design, list of third party accounts.

check: Baseline Azure Policy assignments exist (allowed regions, required tags, approved sizes, no public addresses on machines unless approved).
why_it_matters: Policy enforces the standards without relying on people remembering.

check: Policy compliance is reviewed regularly and exemptions have an owner and an expiry date.
why_it_matters: Permanent exceptions become the standard.

check: Infrastructure as code is the default route for deployment, and portal changes to production are restricted.
why_it_matters: Hand-built environments cannot be reproduced or audited.

check: Decision rights and change process are defined: who approves new subscriptions, networks and exceptions.
why_it_matters: Without them the design drifts through urgent requests.

check: Resource locks or deletion protection are applied to critical shared resources.
why_it_matters: Accidental deletion of a shared service takes down many applications.

check: A central log workspace is designed and platform logs (such as activity logs) are collected.
why_it_matters: Operations and security need one place to look.

check: Monitoring agents or data collection are on migrated machines, with baseline alerts (availability, CPU, memory, disk).
why_it_matters: Machines that moved silently stop being watched if this is skipped.

check: Alerts route to named on-call people with agreed severity and response times, and routing was tested.
why_it_matters: An alert nobody receives is not monitoring.

check: Service health and resource health notifications reach the operations team.
why_it_matters: Provider-side problems must not be discovered from user complaints.

check: Patching and configuration drift management is defined: who patches, when, and how it is verified.
why_it_matters: Moved machines are often out of the patching routine.

check: Operational reports or dashboards exist for the operations team and application owners.
why_it_matters: Owners need to see health without asking IT.

check: A recovery time and recovery point objective is recorded for each application in the wave and mapped to a backup and replication tier.
why_it_matters: Backup design without objectives is guesswork.

check: Backups are configured for migrated machines and databases, with retention agreed and copies held apart from the workload they protect.
why_it_matters: A backup stored beside the thing it protects fails with it.

check: A restore was tested and timed before the first production cutover, and the result recorded.
why_it_matters: An untested backup is a hope.

check: The disaster recovery design (secondary region or alternative) and failover runbook exist, with a test scheduled.
why_it_matters: Moving to a single region without a plan can reduce resilience.

check: The platform itself can be rebuilt: configuration is in code and key and secret stores have recovery protection.
why_it_matters: Losing the landing zone configuration loses every workload's home.

check: On premises backups and the source machine are kept until the Azure copy is proven and the rollback window has closed.
why_it_matters: This is the rollback. See the cutover and rollback template.

check: Budgets and alerts exist for each subscription or workload at agreed thresholds.
why_it_matters: Cost surprises show up after the invoice unless alerts exist.

check: Tag coverage is measured and untagged spend reviewed monthly.
why_it_matters: Untagged spend cannot be charged or challenged.

check: A named owner runs a monthly cost review and acts on right-sizing recommendations.
why_it_matters: Cloud cost drifts upwards without an owner.

check: The decision on commitment discounts (reservations, savings plans) is recorded and made only once running data exists.
why_it_matters: Committing before sizing is known locks in waste.

check: The licence position is confirmed with the vendor or licensing partner, including whether existing licences can be reused (for example through Azure Hybrid Benefit).
why_it_matters: Licensing can change the run cost more than the infrastructure does.

check: A showback or chargeback model is agreed with finance.
why_it_matters: Owners manage cost they can see.

check: Data transfer costs were reviewed for chatty flows between Azure and the remaining on premises estate.
why_it_matters: Egress is rarely in the first business case.

check: An infrastructure as code repository exists with review rules and a pipeline identity with least privilege.
why_it_matters: Automation with excessive rights is a high-value target.

check: The landing zone can be redeployed from code and drift is detected.
why_it_matters: A landing zone that cannot be rebuilt is a single point of failure.

check: Runbooks exist for common operations and for cutover and rollback.
why_it_matters: Runbooks make the 2am version of the job possible.

check: Skills gaps are identified and a training or partner plan is agreed.
why_it_matters: The team that runs it must be able to run it.

check: The support model is defined: who handles incidents on Azure resources, escalation to vendors and the provider, and the support plan decision.
why_it_matters: Unclear ownership extends outages.

check: Migration tooling is in place: an Azure Migrate project and appliance (or equivalent), source access, and discovery data compared with the inventory.
why_it_matters: Discovery finds what the inventory missed.
